origin.description: Reports whether one numeric vector majorizes another.

arguments.name: x,y
arguments.text: Numeric vectors of non-negative entries. They can be compared only when they have the same length and the same sum.

origin.details: x majorizes y when the vectors share a length and a sum and, after both are sorted in increasing order, every partial sum of x is at most the partial sum of y. Two vectors can share a length and a sum and still be unordered: neither majorizes the other.
origin.value: TRUE if x majorizes y, FALSE if the vectors are comparable but x does not majorize y. An error is raised when the lengths or the sums differ.
origin.example:
# generate vectors (of incomes)
x <- c(541, 1463, 2445, 3438, 4437, 5401, 6392, 8304, 11904, 22261)
y <- c(841, 2063, 2445, 3438, 4437, 5401, 6392, 8304, 11304, 21961)
# test whether x majorizes y (TRUE, because y is result of
# Pigou-Dalton-transfers)
major(x,y)

translation.description: Reports whether one numeric vector majorizes another.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Numeric vector of values expected to be non-negative.

arguments.name: y
arguments.text: Numeric vector compared with x. The two can be ordered by majorization only when they have the same length and the same sum.

translation.details: Both arguments are sorted in increasing order. The result is true when the lengths match, the sums match, and cumsum(sort(x)) - cumsum(sort(y)) is entirely less than or equal to zero. That is the statement that x majorizes y. A matching length and sum can still leave the vectors unordered, in which case the result is false. Different lengths or different sums raise ValueError with the message "incomparable arguments".
translation.value: True if x majorizes y, False if the vectors are comparable but x does not majorize y.
